subject.title: Feature request: first-class Telegram reaction triggers for agent wake-up and execution

question: Should Telegram reaction wake and execution semantics be accepted through the shared notificationWake.reactions policy, through a Telegram-specific reaction semantics API, or split across narrower follow-up issues before implementation?
rationale: Current main has only passive reaction system events, and the open candidates make a compatibility-sensitive config/API choice that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Use shared opt-in wake policy
options.body: Resolve and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical wake path, keeping default behavior queued and leaving per-emoji execution/durability to separate issues.

options.title: Sponsor Telegram-specific semantics
options.body: Choose a Telegram reactionSemantics-style API and require explicit config, docs, tests, and live Telegram proof before accepting it.

options.title: Keep the umbrella split
options.body: Leave this issue open only as the Telegram umbrella while narrower issues own wake, prompt guidance, custom emoji, and persistence independently.

recommendation.title: Use shared opt-in wake policy
recommendation.body: Resolve and review https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/83611 as the canonical wake path, keeping default behavior queued and leaving per-emoji execution/durability to separate issues.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete owns the most concrete open shared-policy candidate and has recent Telegram docs/runtime history on the affected surface.
